- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 5–7% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven surges (last 5–7 days of forecast) — increase final 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment > 0.67.
- Model underestimates true price divergence in early 30d (first 5–7 days) — add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
